classification.difficultyReason: Describe intersections and unions of contextual sets and decide whether their memberships overlap.

content.prompt: In each part, describe the sets $A\cap B$ and $A\cup B$. Then state whether or not the sets are disjoint.

children.label: a
children.prompt: $A=\{\text{girls who play winter sport}\}$, $B=\{\text{girls who play summer sport}\}$

answer.short:
$A\cap B=\{\text{girls who play winter and summer sport}\}$.

$A\cup B=\{\text{girls who play winter or summer sport}\}$.

Not disjoint.
answer.worked: The intersection contains girls who play both winter and summer sport. The union contains girls who play winter or summer sport, including those who play both. Some girls play both, so the sets have elements in common and are not disjoint.

answer.short:
$A\cap B=\{\text{singers who sing popular and classical music}\}$.

$A\cup B=\{\text{singers who sing popular or classical music}\}$.

Not disjoint.
answer.worked: The intersection contains singers who sing both popular and classical music. The union contains singers who sing popular or classical music, including those who sing both. Some singers sing both kinds of music, so the sets have elements in common and are not disjoint.

answer.short:
$A\cap B=\varnothing$.

$A\cup B=\{\text{hard- or soft-boiled eggs}\}$.

Disjoint.
answer.worked: An egg cannot be both hard-boiled and soft-boiled, so $A\cap B=\varnothing$. The union contains all hard-boiled and all soft-boiled eggs. The sets have no elements in common, so they are disjoint.
